Fixed in `d23386884`. `pruneSessionStates` still screens files with the async `stat`. For an expired file it now re-checks with `statSync` and removes it with `rmSync` with no await in between, so a state file rewritten while the first stat was pending is kept, as `session-state.test.ts` covers. A write from another process that lands between those two calls can still be lost, because there is no unlink-if-unchanged.

Fixed in `d11e7aca0`. `pruneSessionStates` now removes an expired file through `removeIfUnchanged`: it renames the file aside (atomic, so no write can interleave) and deletes it only if it is still the version whose age was checked (same inode, mtime and size); a version written since goes back with `linkSync`, which fails rather than overwrite a write that landed after the rename. `session-state.test.ts` covers a write after the last check and one that lands while a newer version is held aside.

Fixed in f83618bd27. `begin()` now only stages the new epoch. `activate()` promotes it once the replacement session is resident. Until then the resident session keeps its slot state, viewers and UI chain, and keeps serving invokes. A start that fails releases only its staged epoch, so a failed reopen leaves the working chat's suggestions as they were. `clearPlugin` also takes the epoch now, so a plugin that fails while the replacement is starting can't clear the resident copy.

Covered by "serves the resident session while a same-id start is pending and after it fails" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, plus the staging cases in `store.test.ts` and `service.teardown.test.ts`.

Fixed in 27d4a864de. When a staged start becomes resident and its epoch is no longer the newest minted for the session, `promote` now re-stages it under a fresh epoch and restamps its stored envelopes before anything is emitted. The resident epoch is then always the highest renderers have seen. That covers a later-begun start that registered first, whether it is still resident or has already ended. `PluginUiService.activate` creates the chain under that epoch and returns it, and `LocalRuntimeHost` takes it on for the plugin's later pushes and for teardown.

Covered by "gives the same-id start that registers last the highest epoch, even when it began first" in `local-runtime-host.plugin-ui.test.ts`, and by the two restamp cases in `store.test.ts`.

Valid, and the window is wider than the comment says: `updateSessionStatus` in the persistence service retries a write whose status lock went stale, so when the two writes overlap the in-flight `running` fails its first attempt, re-reads the row and writes `running` on top of `cancelled`. The late writer always wins.

+	private async refreshList(force = false): Promise<void> {

+			return

+			try {
+				void this.recoverAbandonedStarts()

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) {
+					return

+				for (const record of records) {
+					seen.add(record.id)
+					this.upsertRecord(record)
+				}
+				// A record that left the account's list was deleted elsewhere (for
+				// example from the dashboard). Close its connection rather than keep
+				// it in History; the task on screen keeps its host so that opening it
+				// can explain the deletion (see explainConnectFailure).
+				for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+					if (seen.has(id) || this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue
+					this.entries.delete(id)
+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+					void entry.host?.dispose("deleted").catch(() => undefined)
+				}
+				this.pruneRememberedStatuses(seen)

+			} catch (error) {

+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) return
+				if (error instanceof CloudSessionError && error.code === "authentication_required") {

+					// the retained connections that nothing is using. The displayed task
+					// keeps its entry and host: closing them would leave a task on screen
+					// that cannot continue even after the user signs in again, and its
+					// next interaction reports the authentication failure itself.
+					for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {

+					}

+			} finally {
+				if (this.listPromise === listPromise) {
+					this.listPromise = undefined
+				}
+			}
+		})()

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.
+			if (existing.agentStatus && isSettled(existing.agentStatus)) {
+				existing.agentStatus = this.rememberedStatusOf(record)
+			}
+			return existing
+		}

+			record,
+			pinned: 0,
+			agentStatus: this.rememberedStatusOf(record),
+			lastActivityAt: Date.parse(record.updatedAt) || Date.now(),

+		return entry
+	}

+	/** Changes account scope as one boundary: invalidate, detach, dispose, mutate scope, then reopen reads. */

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {

+							reject(
+								new Error(

+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])
+		} finally {
+			clearTimeout(timer)
+		}
+	}

+	private async connect(entry: CloudSessionEntry): Promise<CloudSessionHost> {

+		}

+		const record = entry.record
+		const connection = (async () => {
+			const retainedHost = entry.host
+			const host =
+				retainedHost ??

+					outerSessionId: sessionId,
+					taskId,
+					socketUrl: this.options.cloudSessions.sessionSocketUrl(sessionId),
+					getAuthToken: this.options.getAuthToken,
+					requestToolApproval: this.options.requestToolApproval,
+					telemetry: this.options.telemetry,
+					onStatusChange: (status) => {

+						if (!this.disposed && generation === this.scopeGeneration && this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) {

+						}
+					},
+				}))

+		}

+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)

+			return

+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {

+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.

+	}

+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	/** History rows for every cloud session in the active account scope (cached briefly). */

+		// The pending start's own task row already stands for its sandbox.

+		const entries = [...this.entries.values()].filter((entry) => entry.record.id !== pendingStartSessionId)

+		// A start that settled meanwhile has invalidated History; omitting its row now would be cached as current.
+		if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || pendingStartSessionId !== this.pendingStartSessionId) {
+			return this.listHistoryRecords()

+	async findHistoryRecord(sessionId: string): Promise<SessionHistoryRecord | undefined> {

+			return undefined

+	/** Resolves live status only for cloud rows a caller is about to display. */

+		await this.scopeTransition
+		const generation = this.scopeGeneration
+		const now = Date.now()
+		const visibleIds = [...new Set(sessionIds)].filter(isPersistedCloudSessionId).slice(0, 100)
+		let changed = false
+		const pendingIds = [...visibleIds]
+		const resolveNext = async (): Promise<void> => {
+			for (let sessionId = pendingIds.shift(); sessionId; sessionId = pendingIds.shift()) {
+				const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+				if (!entry || this.statusOf(entry) !== "unknown") continue
+				try {
+					if (entry.connection) {
+						await entry.connection
+						changed = true
+						continue
+					}
+					const lastAttempt = this.statusResolutionAttempts.get(sessionId)
+					if (lastAttempt !== undefined && now - lastAttempt < STATUS_RESOLUTION_RETRY_MS) continue
+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.set(sessionId, now)

+				}
+			}
+		}

+			Array.from({ length: Math.min(STATUS_RESOLUTION_CONCURRENCY, pendingIds.length) }, () => resolveNext()),
+		)

+		}

+	private async refreshUsage(entries: CloudSessionEntry[]): Promise<void> {

+					const usage = await withTimeout(host.getAccumulatedUsage(entry.record.id), USAGE_REFRESH_TIMEOUT_MS)

+	private async refreshList(force = false): Promise<void> {

+		// fetching would attribute old-account rows to the new scope. History
+		// omits cloud rows during the transition; reset refreshes them afterwards.
+		if (this.scopeTransition || this.disposed) return
+		if (!force && Date.now() - this.listFetchedAt < LIST_CACHE_TTL_MS) {
+			return
+		}
+		if (this.listPromise) {
+			return this.listPromise
+		}
+		const generation = this.scopeGeneration
+		let listPromise!: Promise<void>
+		listPromise = (async () => {
+			try {
+				void this.recoverAbandonedStarts()
+				const records = await this.options.cloudSessions.listSessions()
+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) {
+					return
+				}
+				const seen = new Set<string>()
+				for (const record of records) {
+					seen.add(record.id)
+					this.upsertRecord(record)
+				}
+				// A record that left the account's list was deleted elsewhere (for
+				// example from the dashboard). Close its connection rather than keep
+				// it in History; the task on screen keeps its host so that opening it
+				// can explain the deletion (see explainConnectFailure).
+				for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+					if (seen.has(id) || this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue
+					this.entries.delete(id)
+					this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+					void entry.host?.dispose("deleted").catch(() => undefined)
+				}
+				this.pruneRememberedStatuses(seen)
+				this.listFetchedAt = Date.now()
+			} catch (error) {
+				// Reset invalidates both successful responses and failed requests.
+				if (generation !== this.scopeGeneration || this.disposed) return
+				if (error instanceof CloudSessionError && error.code === "authentication_required") {
+					// The account's credentials no longer work. Drop the rows and close
+					// the retained connections that nothing is using. The displayed task
+					// keeps its entry and host: closing them would leave a task on screen
+					// that cannot continue even after the user signs in again, and its
+					// next interaction reports the authentication failure itself.
+					for (const [id, entry] of this.entries) {
+						if (this.isHostInUse(entry)) continue
+						this.entries.delete(id)
+						this.statusResolutionAttempts.delete(id)
+						void entry.host?.dispose("authenticationRequired").catch(() => undefined)
+					}
+				}
+				// Keep the last snapshot; History still renders local tasks.
+				Logger.warn("[CloudSessions] Failed to refresh cloud session list:", error)
+				this.listFetchedAt = Date.now()
+			} finally {
+				if (this.listPromise === listPromise) {
+					this.listPromise = undefined
+				}
+			}
+		})()

+		return listPromise
+	}

+	private upsertRecord(record: CloudSessionRecord): CloudSessionEntry {
+		const existing = this.entries.get(record.id)

+			existing.record = record

+			// settled outcomes against the record just as we do after restart.
+			if (existing.agentStatus && isSettled(existing.agentStatus)) {
+				existing.agentStatus = this.rememberedStatusOf(record)
+			}
+			return existing
+		}

+			record,
+			pinned: 0,
+			agentStatus: this.rememberedStatusOf(record),
+			lastActivityAt: Date.parse(record.updatedAt) || Date.now(),
+		}

+		return entry
+	}

+	/** Changes account scope as one boundary: invalidate, detach, dispose, mutate scope, then reopen reads. */

+				// before a later auth/config refresh failed.

+	private trackScopeOperation<T>(operation: () => Promise<T>): Promise<T> {

+	private async drainScopeOperations(operations: Promise<unknown>[]): Promise<void> {

+								),
+							),
+						SCOPE_DRAIN_TIMEOUT_MS,
+					)
+				}),
+			])

+			clearTimeout(timer)

+	private async connect(entry: CloudSessionEntry): Promise<CloudSessionHost> {

+		const taskId = entry.record.metadata.taskId?.trim()

+			const retainedHost = entry.host
+			const host =
+				retainedHost ??

+					outerSessionId: sessionId,
+					taskId,
+					socketUrl: this.options.cloudSessions.sessionSocketUrl(sessionId),
+					getAuthToken: this.options.getAuthToken,
+					requestToolApproval: this.options.requestToolApproval,
+					telemetry: this.options.telemetry,
+					onStatusChange: (status) => {

+						if (!this.disposed && generation === this.scopeGeneration && this.entries.get(sessionId) === entry) {

+						}
+					},

+		try {
+			return await connection
+		} finally {

+		}
+	}

+	private handleStatusChange(sessionId: string, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {
+		const entry = this.entries.get(sessionId)
+		if (!entry) {
+			return
+		}
+		const previous = entry.agentStatus
+		const now = Date.now()
+		entry.agentStatus = status
+		if (isSettled(status)) {
+			this.rememberStatus(entry.record, status, now)
+		}

+		// change observed while connected moves the task up in History.
+		if (previous !== undefined && previous !== status) {
+			entry.lastActivityAt = now
+		}

+		if (!isDisplayed && previous !== undefined && previous !== status && (status === "completed" || status === "failed")) {
+			this.notifyFinished(entry, status)
+		}
+		this.options.postStateToWebview().catch(() => {})
+	}

+	private notifyFinished(entry: CloudSessionEntry, status: CloudSessionStatus): void {

+	private ensurePolling(): void {

+	private async startCloudTaskInScope(

discussion_comments.comment_body: Not fixing this here. This read-then-attach order dates back to the original cloud runtime commit; it isn't new in this PR. The window is a single `readMessages` round trip, and if the reply lands in it, reopening the task re-reads the transcript and shows it. Buffering events across the read adds a lot of reconciliation code for a narrow, self-healing case.

Implemented in `84db143`.

The response is claimed before the first asynchronous delivery step, so a second submission cannot resolve the same question. It is routed through the normal follow-up path while the claimed response continues delivering its attachments. I kept the session identity check and retained a per-attempt validity token so cancellation, replacement questions, delivery failures, and retries remain safe: an old callback cannot become current again after a retry, and a failed attempt releases only its own claim.

The focused VS Code suites cover the overlap, cancellation, failure/retry, and stale-callback cases and pass; SDK typecheck also passes. The separate display fix keeps the original pending-question text in the submitted event while preserving the expanded model prompt.

Implemented in commit `84db143`.

The pending ask response is now claimed synchronously before attachment preparation begins. While that claim is in flight, another submission cannot resolve the same `ask_question`; it falls through to the normal follow-up path instead. The claim is tied to the individual delivery attempt, so cancellation or replacement of the question invalidates older callbacks, while a delivery error releases only its own claim and leaves the original response retryable.

I added regressions covering overlapping text and attachment submissions, cancellation during delivery, delivery failure followed by a retry, and stale `isCurrent` callbacks after a replacement question. The focused VS Code suites pass (231 tests total), and the SDK typecheck passes.

🟡 **bug** (medium)

The `findLastIndex(..., m => m.say === "checkpoint_created")` lookup now runs inside the background promise (after `commit()` resolves) instead of while this call is still the newest checkpoint. Since commits are no longer awaited, two `saveCheckpoint()` calls can overlap — the agent routinely runs several tools back to back, and the comment you added notes a commit can take seconds on large shadow git repos. When the earlier commit resolves, this lookup finds the *newest* `checkpoint_created` message and writes its hash there, so the message that actually belongs to that commit stays without a `lastCheckpointHash`; if the commits resolve out of order, a message can even end up carrying a different checkpoint's hash. Both cases corrupt the per-message hash that 'Restore checkpoint' and `doesLatestTaskCompletionHaveNewChanges()` rely on.

**建议**: Resolve the target message synchronously instead of by re-searching later: right after `await this.say("checkpoint_created")` capture the message index/`ts` of the message you just created, and inside the `.then()` callback update exactly that captured message (re-validate it still exists). Alternatively serialize commits by chaining/storing the in-flight promise.

Valid — and together with the afterModel finding below, this made the pattern undeniable: five windows of the same class means the design is wrong, not the placement. Recording the reason on every finish event and chasing failure windows with resets cannot terminate, because any callback that throws between a finish and the next reset inherits stale state.

So I inverted it rather than patch a sixth window. Nothing is recorded on finish events anymore; the reason is set immediately before each finish-reason-driven throw (empty turn, max-tokens with no tool calls, provider error with no tool calls). Nothing can interleave between a synchronous set-and-throw and the run-level catch, so `sdk.error` can never pick up a reason from a request that did not cause the failure — this window, the afterModel one, and any future callback-throw site are all closed by construction. Both reset sites are deleted; net less state juggling than before.

Regression tests added for both new windows (each verified to fail on the reset-based design); the four earlier stale-attribution tests now pin the property under the new mechanism. Agents suite 76/76.

`request()` coalesces a newer request into `pending`, but it doesn't invalidate an already-active rebuild for the same reason — `cancellationGeneration` only moves in `cancel()` (line 40). So the active run's `isCurrent()` stays `true`, and once it finishes the newer request rebuilds the session again.

There's a correctness window here, not just redundant work. If the active rebuild has already snapshotted its config when the newer setting arrives, it installs the superseded one; and for checkpoint rebuilds it can replay a deferred follow-up from the shared `checkpointTransition` before the newer rebuild applies the latest setting — so a real message can run under the old checkpoint config.

I don't think bumping the generation here is a self-contained fix: the transition object is shared between the active and queued requests, and an invalidated rebuild returning from `replaceActiveSession()` can still clear `this.checkpointTransition` and stop the replacement. Either make a same-reason request explicitly supersede the active run with the transition ownership handled to match, or rename `isCurrent()` so it's clear it only means "not cancelled". A scheduler test for requesting a reason while that reason is actively rebuilding would pin whichever contract you pick.

Thanks — you were right on both counts, and the second one hid a real defect.

`isCurrent()` in a78223a means exactly "no newer request for the same reason has arrived": `request()` stamps a per-reason generation, and a running rebuild's context reads it live. `cancel()` and the per-reason cancellation generation are gone; nothing could reach them because `runTaskTransition` waits for the drain first.

The shared `checkpointTransition` is gone too. Holding a follow-up outside Core's queue meant nothing rendered it: a message typed during a turn after toggling Checkpoints vanished from the chat until the turn ended (this is what the e2e was failing on across all three CI platforms). Follow-ups now always go to Core's queue. The scheduler treats a session with queued prompts as busy, since Core drains the queue the instant a turn ends, and a send that settles after Core already started the next queued turn no longer flips the session idle. There is a scheduler test for a same-reason request during an active rebuild, and coordinator tests for supersession before replacement.
